source.title: Towards mechanistic understanding in a data-driven weather model: internal activations reveal interpretable physical features

record.file_problem: none; the full paper, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper motivates SAE-based feature analysis partly by the problem of polysemantic neurons, but does not test whether individual neurons respond to unrelated concepts. Its neuron probes measure prediction of single weather-event labels, not polysemanticity as defined in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses polysemantic neurons as motivation and compares single-neuron and SAE-feature probes for weather-event labels. Those probe results do not measure responses to multiple unrelated inputs, nor any other version’s stated behavior. The probe outcomes are recorded as related findings under versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The paper mentions polysemantic neurons only as background motivation for using SAEs in GraphCast. It never measures whether any neuron responds to several unrelated inputs, its share of such neurons, or their causes. Its neuron-level results are single-label probe F1 scores for weather events, a different construct. It does not rely on polysemanticity as a tool whose performance it reports, so T6 (cites only) fits better than T4.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: SAEs on GraphCast's layer-8 node embeddings yield interpretable physical features (TCs, ARs, sea ice, diurnal/seasonal, grid-locked artifacts), and amplifying or attenuating a TC feature changes storm strength in a largely physically consistent way. The authors make no claim about neuron polysemanticity beyond motivation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SAE feature discovery, sparse event probes, and feature modification in a weather model; it does not reproduce the original neuron-level image-classifier analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that TC probe performance varies with SAE hyperparameter choices; intermediate latent sizes nl=2048 and 4096 seem optimal. It hypothesizes feature splitting at larger dictionary sizes. These are feature-probe results, not tests of polysemanticity.

fits_no_version.finding: In GraphCast layer 8, the best SAE feature probe reaches F1 0.48 for tropical-cyclone masks versus 0.01 for the best single neuron. For atmospheric rivers, a neuron probe reaches F1 0.30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a GNN weather model, single neurons can be uninformative for some physical events (TCs) while SAE features isolate them; for other events (ARs), neurons are competitive.

record.problems: The reported neuron-probe results concern prediction of individual event labels and do not establish whether neurons respond to multiple unrelated concepts. The text gives no uncertainty estimates for these probe scores.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained: the paper’s other reported results concern SAE features, feature modification, physical consistency, or weather-event behavior, and do not measure any claim version’s polysemanticity behavior.

untested.parts: No vision classifiers and no multi-concept neuron responses.
No transformer language models or MLP neuron surveys.
Superposition is not tested; SAEs are applied, not used to test the cause.
No tests of initialization, regularization or noise as causes.
No comparison of architectures or activation functions for polysemantic-neuron prevalence.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T4/uses_without_test is downgraded to T6/cites_only. Polysemanticity appears in one sentence of Section 2 as motivation. Neurons are never characterized as responding to multiple concepts.

versions.untested_parts: No test of vision models or neurons responding to multiple unrelated image inputs.
No transformer language models, MLP neuron survey, or token/context polysemanticity measure.
No test of superposition or feature capacity pressure as a cause.
No test of initialization, regularization, or training noise as causes of polysemanticity without capacity pressure.
No comparison of activation functions, architectures, or regularization for polysemantic-neuron prevalence or performance cost.
No investigation of whether purportedly polysemantic neurons share a coherent feature or job.
No comparison of activation ranges or explanation-scoring methods for classifying neurons as polysemantic.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.stage_stated: trained on 40 years of ERA5 reanalysis data
rows.operation_detail: Logistic probe using SAE feature activations to predict tropical-cyclone mask presence; best reported feature probe.
rows.measure: F1 score for predicting TC mask presence
rows.note: This measures event-label prediction by an SAE feature, not whether neurons respond to unrelated concepts.
rows.check: This is an SAE feature probe, the study's own method, not a neuron polysemanticity measure. Arguably it is a selection value (best feature across SAEs), not a result row.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.stage_stated: trained on 40 years of ERA5 reanalysis data
rows.operation_detail: Logistic probe using neuron activations to predict tropical-cyclone mask presence; best reported neuron probe.
rows.measure: F1 score for predicting TC mask presence
rows.note: The paper describes this as essentially a randomized predictor. A single event-label probe does not measure polysemanticity.
rows.check: A low single-neuron F1 for TC detection shows the neuron is uninformative for TCs, not that it responds to unrelated concepts.

rows.subject: GraphCast
rows.stage_stated: trained on 40 years of ERA5 reanalysis data
rows.operation_detail: Probe using neuron activations to predict atmospheric-river presence.
rows.measure: F1 score for predicting AR presence
rows.note: The authors say this is competitive relative to SAE probes, though worse than all but one. It is an event-label probe, not a measure of unrelated meanings.
rows.check: Neuron AR probe F1 of 0.30 bears on neuron informativeness, not polysemanticity. The model is a GNN weather model, not any kind of system named in the versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
